title: Are you congruent?
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you do every day that points at what you say you want?

groups.heading: You can't just have a floating goal

lines.text: A student told of a conversation with a friend on a long drive. I asked him: define what success looks like to you. When you wake up in the morning, what do you see around you? Then we can reverse engineer it into a plan.

He said he would like to travel around the world, surfing and playing music. I asked what that requires. About a hundred thousand dollars a year of passive income, he said. So what are you doing right now to get that? He froze.
To get to that goal, the student said, you can't just have a floating goal. Hoping your life will intersect with it, some people get lucky. It is one in a billion, like winning the lottery.
99% of the time, the student said, what people do every day is incongruent with the goal. Which means a 99% chance they won't achieve it, unless they hit the lottery.
And I think that is the word, I said. Congruence. Are you congruent with your financial goals and your personal goals? Are you in the realm of reality, making it happen?

The student said: I see commitments get made, and for a day or two or three you stay congruent. Then it falls off. The biggest thing I try to figure out as a leader is how to help people be consistent and congruent day to day.
It comes down to consistency, I said. It comes down to habits. It comes down to little tiny things.

Failure is not one catastrophic event, I said. It is a lot of tiny little bad decisions that you made consistently that led you to the failure. Success is the same. It is a lot of little decisions that you make consistently well.
Getting up in the morning, going to the gym, not eating junk food: all those little things contribute to success and failure, I said.
I said I am infamous for looking into people's cars. A messy car, I say, is a sample of what is inside your brain. A messy house, a messy room: the clutter is relevant.

The more focused you are during your day, keeping your eye on daily objectives that lead you to the long term, the better, I said. A lot of us make a decision one day: today I'm going to be a world champion. Then two months go by, and you forgot about that decision. You didn't train hard every day.
Is what you do every day congruent with your goal?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what success looks like for you: what you see when you wake up.
Write what that requires: money, time, people.
Write what you do every day that points at it, and what does not.
Write one tiny daily decision you will make consistently this week.
Write one thing to clear up: a car, a desk, a room.

check.q: What word did I use for matching your daily actions to your goal?
What did I say success and failure are made of?
choices: A lot of tiny decisions made consistently

check.q: What did I say a messy car is a sample of?

recap: Success and failure are made of tiny daily decisions. Be congruent with your goal.
